questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A student writes the polynomial P(x) = 3x³ − 5x² + 2x − 7.

(i) What is the degree of P(x)?
(ii) Identify the leading coefficient and the constant term.
(iii) Is P(x) a polynomial in x²? Justify.
(iv) Evaluate P(2).
questions.answer:
(i) The highest exponent of x is 3, so degree = 3.
(ii) Leading coefficient (of the highest degree term) = 3. Constant term = −7.
(iii) No. A polynomial in x² has only EVEN powers of x. Here P contains x³ and x, both odd powers.
(iv) P(2) = 3(8) − 5(4) + 2(2) − 7 = 24 − 20 + 4 − 7 = 1.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Let P(x) = x² + 5x + 6 and Q(x) = x² − 4.

(i) Find P(x) + Q(x).
(ii) Find P(x) − Q(x).
(iii) Find P(x) × Q(x).
(iv) What is the degree of the product?
questions.answer:
(i) P + Q = 2x² + 5x + 2.
(ii) P − Q = (x² + 5x + 6) − (x² − 4) = 5x + 10.
(iii) P · Q = (x² + 5x + 6)(x² − 4) = x⁴ − 4x² + 5x³ − 20x + 6x² − 24 = x⁴ + 5x³ + 2x² − 20x − 24.
(iv) Degree of product = degree(P) + degree(Q) = 2 + 2 = 4 ✓.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Divide P(x) = 2x³ + 3x² − x − 6 by D(x) = x − 1.

(i) State the remainder theorem.
(ii) Use it to compute the remainder when P(x) is divided by (x − 1).
(iii) Is (x − 1) a factor of P(x)? Justify.
(iv) Carry out the polynomial long division and write quotient + remainder.
questions.answer:
(i) When a polynomial P(x) is divided by (x − a), the remainder equals P(a).
(ii) Remainder = P(1) = 2 + 3 − 1 − 6 = −2.
(iii) No — for (x − 1) to be a factor, the remainder must be 0, but it's −2. So (x − 1) is NOT a factor.
(iv) Long division: P(x) ÷ (x − 1).
  2x³ ÷ x = 2x². Multiply: 2x²(x−1) = 2x³ − 2x². Subtract: 3x² − (−2x²) = 5x². Bring down: 5x² − x.
  5x² ÷ x = 5x. Multiply: 5x(x−1) = 5x² − 5x. Subtract: 4x. Bring down: 4x − 6.
  4x ÷ x = 4. Multiply: 4(x − 1) = 4x − 4. Subtract: −2.
  Quotient = 2x² + 5x + 4, remainder = −2. So P(x) = (x − 1)(2x² + 5x + 4) − 2.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Let P(x) = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6.

(i) Check if x = 1 is a zero of P(x).
(ii) Check if x = 2 is a zero of P(x).
(iii) Check if x = 3 is a zero of P(x).
(iv) Hence factorise P(x) completely.
questions.answer:
(i) P(1) = 1 − 6 + 11 − 6 = 0. So x = 1 IS a zero.
(ii) P(2) = 8 − 24 + 22 − 6 = 0. So x = 2 IS a zero.
(iii) P(3) = 27 − 54 + 33 − 6 = 0. So x = 3 IS a zero.
(iv) Three roots × degree 3 polynomial ⇒ P(x) = (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3). Verify: expand to confirm matches x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 ✓.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

The polynomial P(x) = ax² + bx + c has zeros α and β.

(i) State the sum-and-product-of-roots formulas for a quadratic.
(ii) If P(x) = 2x² − 5x + 3, find sum of zeros and product of zeros.
(iii) Verify by finding the zeros explicitly.
(iv) Construct a quadratic whose zeros are 2 and -3.
questions.answer:
(i) Sum α + β = −b/a; Product αβ = c/a.
(ii) Here a = 2, b = −5, c = 3. Sum = 5/2; Product = 3/2.
(iii) Solve 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0: x = (5 ± √(25 − 24))/4 = (5 ± 1)/4. So x = 3/2 or 1. Sum = 3/2 + 1 = 5/2 ✓; Product = (3/2)(1) = 3/2 ✓.
(iv) A quadratic with zeros 2 and -3: (x − 2)(x − (−3)) = (x − 2)(x + 3) = x² + x − 6.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Expand (2x + 3y)³ using the identity (a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³.

(i) Identify a and b.
(ii) Write each of the four terms explicitly.
(iii) Sum to get the expansion.
(iv) Apply the same identity to expand (x − 2y)³.
questions.answer:
(i) a = 2x, b = 3y.
(ii) a³ = (2x)³ = 8x³. 3a²b = 3(4x²)(3y) = 36x²y. 3ab² = 3(2x)(9y²) = 54xy². b³ = 27y³.
(iii) (2x + 3y)³ = 8x³ + 36x²y + 54xy² + 27y³.
(iv) (x − 2y)³ = x³ − 3·x²·(2y) + 3·x·(2y)² − (2y)³ = x³ − 6x²y + 12xy² − 8y³.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A classmate claims '(a + b)² = a² + b² always.'

(i) Test the claim with a = 2 and b = 3.
(ii) Identify the missing term.
(iii) State the correct identity for (a + b)².
(iv) For what specific values of a, b would (a + b)² = a² + b² actually hold?
questions.answer:
(i) (2 + 3)² = 25. 2² + 3² = 4 + 9 = 13. So 25 ≠ 13. Claim is FALSE.
(ii) The missing term is 2ab = 2·2·3 = 12. (And 13 + 12 = 25 ✓.)
(iii) Correct identity: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².
(iv) (a + b)² = a² + b² ⟺ 2ab = 0 ⟺ a = 0 or b = 0. So the claim holds only when one of them is zero.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

If α and β are zeros of x² − 7x + 10 = 0:

(i) Find α + β and αβ.
(ii) Find α² + β².
(iii) Find α³ + β³.
(iv) Find 1/α + 1/β.

Read the passage and answer the questions.

The area of a rectangle is given by (x² + 7x + 10) square units.

(i) Factorise x² + 7x + 10.
(ii) Hence give possible dimensions of the rectangle.
(iii) If the perimeter is 14 + 4x, find the value of x for which the perimeter is 30.
(iv) For that x, what is the area?
questions.answer:
(i) x² + 7x + 10 = (x + 2)(x + 5).
(ii) Length × breadth = (x + 5)(x + 2). So dimensions can be (x + 5) and (x + 2) units.
(iii) Perimeter = 14 + 4x = 30 ⇒ 4x = 16 ⇒ x = 4.
(iv) Area = (4 + 5)(4 + 2) = 9·6 = 54 square units.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Determine k so that (x − 2) is a factor of P(x) = x³ + kx² − 4x − 12.

(i) State the factor theorem.
(ii) Apply it to find k.
(iii) For that k, factorise P(x) fully.
(iv) List all the zeros of P(x).
questions.answer:
(i) (x − a) is a factor of P(x) iff P(a) = 0.
(ii) P(2) = 8 + 4k − 8 − 12 = 4k − 12 = 0 ⇒ k = 3.
(iii) With k = 3: P(x) = x³ + 3x² − 4x − 12. We know (x − 2) is a factor. Divide: x³ + 3x² − 4x − 12 = (x − 2)(x² + 5x + 6) = (x − 2)(x + 2)(x + 3).
(iv) Zeros: x = 2, x = −2, x = −3.
